questions.question: A fruit seller sold 200 kg of grapes at ₹15 per kg and 100 kg of oranges at ₹10 per kg. Find his total earnings.

• To formulate the framework, **B.N. Rau** traveled to the **USA**, **Canada**, **Ireland**, and the **United Kingdom** to consult with constitutional experts and jurists, including **Justice Felix Frankfurter** of the US Supreme Court.
 
• The **Drafting Committee**, led by **Dr. B.R. Ambedkar**, utilized **B.N. Rau’s** preliminary draft as the base document to refine and finalize the ultimate text of the Constitution.
 
• Beyond his work in India, he was an eminent jurist who also assisted in drafting the **Constitution of Burma** (Myanmar) in **1947** and served as a judge at the **International Court of Justice** in **The Hague**.

questions.question: Santhal Dance is predominantly performed during which occasion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harvest festivals and religious ceremonies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Santhal dance** is a vibrant and ancient folk dance performed by the **Santhal tribe**, which is one of the largest **Scheduled Tribes** in India, primarily settled in **Jharkhand**, **West Bengal**, **Odisha**, and **Bihar**.
 
• This traditional dance is deeply connected to the agrarian lifestyle of the community and is predominantly performed during **harvest festivals** to express gratitude to the gods and nature for a successful yield.
 
• The most significant occasion for this dance is the **Sohrai festival**, celebrated in the month of **October or November** (after the Kharif harvest), where men and women dance together to the rhythmic beats of traditional drums.
 
• It is also performed during **religious ceremonies** such as **Baha** (the flower festival), which marks the spring season and the arrival of the **Sal** blossoms, honoring the supreme deity **Marang Buru**.
 
• The dance movements are characterized by synchronized steps where dancers form **semi-circles** or **lines**, often holding hands or waist-to-waist, symbolizing **communal harmony** and social cohesion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Santhal Musical Instruments**:

 
 
• **Madal**: A traditional two-headed drum made of clay or wood, which serves as the primary rhythmic heartbeat of the dance.
 
• **Tiriao**: A bamboo flute used to provide melodic accompaniment to the percussion.
 
• **Dhamsa**: A large kettle drum used to add depth and intensity to the performance.
 
 
 
• **Santhal Tribe Heritage**:
 
 
• They follow the **Sarna religion**, which is based on the worship of **nature spirits** and sacred groves known as **Jaher**.
 
• Their language, **Santhali**, is written in the **Ol Chiki** script, which was developed by **Pandit Raghunath Murmu** in 1925.
 
 
 
• **Other Festivals**:
 
 
• **Karam Festival**: Observed to seek blessings for the protection of crops and the well-being of the family.
 
• **Erok-Sim**: A ritual ceremony performed during the sowing of seeds at the start of the monsoon.

questions.question: Tippani dance is traditionally performed during which occasions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Weddings and festivals**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tippani dance** is a prominent folk dance originating from the **Saurashtra** region of **Gujarat**, particularly associated with the coastal towns of **Chorwad** and **Veraval**.
 
• The dance is traditionally performed by the women of the **Koli** and **Bhil** communities, who originally developed these rhythmic movements while working as laborers to level the ground during the construction of houses and forts.
 
• While it has its roots in manual labor, the performance has evolved into a celebratory art form conducted during significant social and cultural events, such as **weddings** and major **Hindu festivals** like **Holi** and **Diwali**.
 
• The performance is characterized by the use of the **Tippani stick**, a long wooden pole roughly **175 cm** in length with a heavy square wooden or iron block (called a **Garbo**) attached at the base to strike the floor.
 
• The dancers arrange themselves in two rows and strike the floor in a synchronized, rhythmic pattern, creating a unique sound that serves as both music and a display of physical coordination and endurance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Instruments and Music**:

 
 
• The rhythmic thumping of the **Tippani** is accompanied by folk instruments like the **Zanz**, **Manjira** (cymbals), **Tabla**, and **Dhol** (drum) to maintain a steady tempo.
 
• The **Turi** and **Shehnai** are also frequently used to provide melodic accompaniment to the percussive nature of the dance.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Context**:
 
 
• Unlike purely **Religious rituals** that are confined to temples, Tippani is a social dance that brings the community together in public squares or household courtyards.
 
• The costumes worn are traditional Gujarati attire, including the **Ghagra-Choli** for women, often embellished with mirrors and vibrant embroidery typical of the **Saurashtra** folk style.
 
• It is often compared to other work-related folk dances, but it stands out due to its high energy and the **percussive floor-striking** technique which is rare in other Indian folk traditions.

questions.question: The Satpura Range is located in which part of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Satpura Range** is a major mountain system located in **Central India**, forming a significant part of the Indian peninsula's geographic backbone.
 
• Geographically, it extends in an **east-west direction** across the states of **Gujarat**, **Maharashtra**, **Madhya Pradesh**, and **Chhattisgarh**.
 
• The range is situated between two major west-flowing rivers: the **Narmada River** to the north and the **Tapti River** to the south.
 
• It runs parallel to the **Vindhya Range**, and together they create a natural divide between the **Indo-Gangetic Plain** of Northern India and the **Deccan Plateau** of the south.
 
• The name 'Satpura' is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Sapta' (seven) and 'Pura' (mountains), signifying the **seven folds** or hills that constitute the range.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geological Characteristics:**

 
 
• The Satpura Range is classified as a **block mountain** (horst), formed due to tectonic activity that created **rift valleys** (graben) on either side.
 
• The range is composed primarily of **basaltic rocks** in the west, while its eastern sections are made of **Gondwana formations** and metamorphic rocks.
 
 
 
• **Highest Peak and Sub-ranges:**
 
 
• **Dhupgarh**, located in the **Mahadeo Hills** near the hill station of Pachmarhi, is the highest peak of the Satpura Range, standing at **1,350 meters**.
 
• The range includes several distinct hilly tracts such as the **Rajpipla Hills**, **Gawilgarh Hills**, and the **Maikal Range**.
 
 
 
• **River Systems and Biodiversity:**
 
 
• The **Amarkantak Plateau**, where the Satpura and Vindhya ranges meet, is the source of the **Narmada** and **Son** rivers.
 
• The range is home to rich deciduous forests and famous tiger reserves, including **Kanha National Park**, **Satpura National Park**, and **Pench National Park**.

• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a composite statistical tool used to measure a country's overall achievement in its social and economic dimensions, shifting the focus from purely economic growth to human-centric development.
 
• It was created by Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and Indian Nobel laureate **Amartya Sen** and has been published annually by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** since **1990**.
 
• The index is calculated using three basic dimensions: a **Long and healthy life**, **Knowledge**, and a **Decent standard of living**.
 
• The **Health** dimension is assessed by **Life expectancy at birth**, which serves as a proxy for the quality of a nation's healthcare system, nutrition, and environmental safety.
 
• The **Knowledge** or **Education** dimension is measured through a combination of the **Mean years of schooling** for adults aged 25 years and older and the **Expected years of schooling** for children of school-entering age.
 
• The **Standard of Living** is quantified using **Gross National Income (GNI) per capita** adjusted for **Purchasing Power Parity (PPP)** in US dollars to account for differences in the cost of living across countries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Methodology and Scoring**:

 
 
• HDI values range between **0 and 1**; a score closer to 1 indicates a higher level of human development.
 
• Countries are categorized into four tiers: **Very High** (0.800 and above), **High** (0.700–0.799), **Medium** (0.550–0.699), and **Low Human Development** (below 0.550).
 
• The final index is the **geometric mean** of the normalized indices for each of the three dimensions, ensuring that poor performance in one area is not masked by high performance in another.
 
 
 
• **Extended Indices**:
 
 
• To address criticisms of the HDI, the UNDP introduced the **Inequality-adjusted HDI (IHDI)** in 2010 to account for how achievements are distributed among the population.
 
• Other related metrics include the **Gender Inequality Index (GII)**, which measures gender-based disadvantages, and the **Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI)**, which identifies overlapping deprivations.
 
• While **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** measures economic output, HDI is considered a more holistic indicator as it incorporates social indicators like **literacy** and **longevity**.

questions.question: The tilt of Earth's axis varies between 22.1° and 24.5° over 41,000 years (Milankovitch cycles). How does this variation affect Earth?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Greater tilt increases seasonal contrast**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Axial tilt**, also known as **obliquity**, is the angle between Earth's rotational axis and its orbital plane, currently measuring approximately **23.5 degrees**.
 
• The tilt fluctuates between **22.1 degrees** and **24.5 degrees** over a cycle of roughly **41,000 years**, a phenomenon identified by Serbian scientist **Milutin Milankovitch**.
 
• When the tilt is at its maximum (**24.5 degrees**), each hemisphere receives more direct **solar radiation** during its summer and significantly less during its winter, which **increases seasonal contrast**.
 
• A greater tilt results in hotter summers and colder winters because the higher latitudes are oriented more directly toward or away from the **Sun** during solstices.
 
• Conversely, a minimum tilt of **22.1 degrees** leads to milder seasons; cooler summers in this phase often prevent winter snow from melting entirely, facilitating the growth of **ice sheets** and triggering **glaciation**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Milankovitch Cycles** include two other primary variations:

 
 
• **Eccentricity**: This refers to the shape of Earth's orbit around the Sun, which shifts from nearly circular to mildly elliptical over **100,000-year** and **400,000-year** cycles, affecting the total **insolation** received.
 
• **Precession**: Often called the Earth's 'wobble', this **26,000-year cycle** changes the orientation of the axis, determining which hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun at **perihelion** (closest approach) or **aphelion** (farthest point).
 
 
 
• **Orbital Speed**: The speed at which Earth travels is governed by **Kepler's Second Law** and is influenced by **eccentricity** (distance from the Sun), not the tilt of the axis.
 
• **Magnetic Field**: Earth's magnetism is generated by the **geodynamo** effect in the **outer core** and is independent of the orbital **obliquity** cycles.

questions.question: Which type of action is heartbeat?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Involuntary action**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Involuntary actions** are biological processes or movements that occur without the conscious control or will of an individual.
 
• The **heartbeat** is classified as an involuntary action because it is performed automatically by the body to ensure continuous **blood circulation**, requiring no deliberate thought.
 
• These functions are primarily regulated by the **Autonomic Nervous System (ANS)**, which manages internal organ operations.
 
• The **Medulla Oblongata**, situated in the **hindbrain**, acts as the primary control center for regulating the **heart rate**, **breathing**, and **blood pressure**.
 
• The rhythmic contraction of the heart is initiated by the **Sinoatrial (SA) node**, often referred to as the **natural pacemaker**, located in the right atrium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reflex Action**

 
 
• This is a rapid, spontaneous response to a stimulus, such as the **knee-jerk reflex** or **blinking** of eyes.
 
• It is usually controlled by the **spinal cord** to protect the body from immediate harm.
 
 
 
• **Voluntary Action**
 
 
• These actions are under the direct control of the **cerebrum** and involve conscious decision-making.
 
• Examples include **writing**, **cycling**, and **dancing**.
 
 
 
• **Cardiac Muscles**
 
 
• The heart is composed of unique **striated muscles** that are **myogenic** in nature, meaning they can initiate contraction without external nerve impulses.
 
• These muscles never fatigue, allowing the heart to beat approximately **72 times per minute** throughout a person's lifetime.

questions.question: Which of the following is the primary function of lysosomes in a cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Waste disposal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lysosomes** are membrane-bound vesicular structures formed by the process of packaging in the **Golgi apparatus**.
 
• They serve as the **waste disposal system** of the cell by digesting foreign materials, such as bacteria and food, as well as **worn-out cell organelles**.
 
• These organelles contain a variety of **hydrolytic enzymes** (including lipases, proteases, and carbohydrases) that are capable of breaking down all major classes of biological macromolecules.
 
• The enzymes within a lysosome are optimally active at an **acidic pH** (approximately 4.5 to 5.0), which is maintained by **proton pumps** in the lysosomal membrane.
 
• In the event of cellular damage or malfunction, lysosomes may burst, leading to the **autolysis** or self-digestion of the cell; for this reason, they are famously known as the **suicide bags** of the cell.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Energy production**:

 
 
• This is the primary role of the **mitochondria**, often referred to as the **powerhouse of the cell**.
 
• Mitochondria produce **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)** through the process of **oxidative phosphorylation** during cellular respiration.
 
 
 
• **Protein synthesis**:
 
 
• This process is carried out by **ribosomes**, which can be found floating freely in the **cytoplasm** or attached to the **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)**.
 
• The **nucleolus** within the nucleus is responsible for the synthesis of ribosomal RNA (rRNA).
 
 
 
• **Storage of lipids**:
 
 
• The **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)** is the major site for the **synthesis and storage of lipids** and steroid hormones.
 
• In specialized animal cells, lipids are stored in large quantities within **adipocytes** (fat cells) in the form of **triglycerides**.

questions.question: 96 - 41 + 27 + 36 ÷ 3 + (19 of 1) - 22 = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Solve **(19 of 1) = 19** and **36 ÷ 3 = 12** first.

Rewrite: 96 − 41 + 27 + 12 + 19 − 22

Sum positives: 96 + 27 + 12 + 19 = 154

Sum negatives: 41 + 22 = 63

Final: 154 − 63 = 91

**∴ The correct answer is 91.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Expression:** 96 − 41 + 27 + 36 ÷ 3 + (19 of 1) − 22

Follow the **BODMAS** rule (Bracket, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction):

⇒ 96 − 41 + 27 + 36 ÷ 3 + 19 − 22 (Solving **Of**: 19 × 1 = 19)

⇒ 96 − 41 + 27 + 12 + 19 − 22 (Solving **Division**: 36 ÷ 3 = 12)

⇒ (96 + 27 + 12 + 19) − 41 − 22 (Rearranging **Positive** terms)

⇒ 154 − 41 − 22 (Performing **Addition**)

⇒ 154 − 63 (Performing **Subtraction** of negative totals)

⇒ 91

**∴ The correct answer is 91.**

BODMAS / VBODMAS Rule

It defines the sequence: **V** (Vinculum), **B** (Brackets), **O** (Of), **D** (Division), **M** (Multiplication), **A** (Addition), **S** (Subtraction).

The 'Of' Operator

The **'Of'** operator is mathematically equivalent to **multiplication** but must be evaluated before division and standard multiplication.

Addition and Subtraction Priority

Addition and subtraction have the **same level of precedence** and can be solved from left to right after all higher-priority operations are complete.

questions.question: The illumination of a lamp on a surface varies directly as its power and inversely as the square of its distance from the surface. If a 60 W lamp placed 2 m above a desk provides an illumination of 15 lux, find the illumination when a 100 W lamp is placed 3 m above the desk.

I₂ / I₁ = (P₂ / P₁) × (d₁ / d₂)²

I₂ / 15 = (5 / 3) × (4 / 9) ⇒ I₂ = 15 × 20 / 27 = 300 / 27

Inverse Square Law

Luminous Flux vs. Illumination

Cross-Multiplication Rule

Same Difference Rule

questions.question: Sum of the diagonals of a rhombus is 62 cm. Area of this rhombus is 336 square cm. What is the side (in cm) of the rhombus?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **Sum of Diagonals (d₁ + d₂)** = 62 cm and **Area** = 336 cm².

Relationship between **Side (a)** and **Diagonals**: 4a² = d₁² + d₂².

We know (d₁ + d₂)² = d₁² + d₂² + 2d₁d₂ = 4a² + 4 × Area.

62² = 4a² + 4 × 336 ⇒ 3844 = 4a² + 1344.

4a² = 2500 ⇒ a² = 625 ⇒ a = 25 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of diagonals (d₁ + d₂) = 62 cm

Area of rhombus = 336 cm²

**Formula Used:**

Area of Rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

Side of Rhombus (a) = √[(d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5ec809795573157a8f7737ee616de8f03a595d393467b093eec890e5c0e3bb67.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂ = 336

⇒ d₁ × d₂ = 672

⇒ We know: (d₁ + d₂)² = d₁² + d₂² + 2d₁d₂

⇒ 62² = d₁² + d₂² + 2(672)

⇒ 3844 = d₁² + d₂² + 1344

⇒ d₁² + d₂² = 3844 − 1344 = 2500

⇒ For a rhombus, 4a² = d₁² + d₂²

⇒ 4a² = 2500

⇒ a² = 2500 ÷ 4 = 625

⇒ a = √625 = 25 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 25 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rhombus

All four sides are equal, and diagonals bisect each other at right angles (90°).

Perimeter of Rhombus

The perimeter is given by 4 × side (a).

Pythagorean Relation

The side and half-diagonals form a right-angled triangle: a² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)².

questions.question: The adjacent angles of a parallelogram are in the ratio of 1:3. What are the measure (in degrees) of the larger angle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **parallelogram**, the sum of **adjacent angles** is always 180°.

Total ratio parts = 1 + 3 = 4 units.

4 units ⇒ 180°

1 unit ⇒ 180° ÷ 4 = 45°

Larger angle (3 units) ⇒ 3 × 45° = 135°.

**∴ The correct answer is 135°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **adjacent angles** = 1 : 3

**Formula used:**

Sum of **adjacent angles** in a **parallelogram** = 180° (Supplementary angles property)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/514b1737a1aa53e59b16c1f16cf47d6f4e77f119deec68fac8cf319e83b8e1ff.png] 

Let the two **adjacent angles** be 1x and 3x.

⇒ 1x + 3x = 180°

⇒ 4x = 180°

⇒ x = 180° ÷ 4

⇒ x = 45°

⇒ Smaller angle = 1 × 45° = 45°

⇒ Larger angle = 3 × 45° = 135°

**∴ The correct answer is 135°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Parallelogram

Opposite angles are **equal**, and consecutive (adjacent) angles are **supplementary** (sum to 180°).

Diagonal Properties

The **diagonals** of a parallelogram **bisect** each other but are not necessarily equal in length unless it is a rectangle.

Angle Sum Property

The sum of all four interior angles of any **quadrilateral**, including a parallelogram, is always 360°.

questions.question: What is the Least Common Multiple of 4/7, 8/14 and 12/21?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Simplify all **fractions** to their **lowest terms** before calculation.

4/7 is already in simplest form.

8/14 → 4/7 (dividing by 2) and 12/21 → 4/7 (dividing by 3).

Since all fractions are now 4/7, their **LCM** is 4/7.

**∴ The correct answer is 4/7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Fractions:** 4/7, 8/14, and 12/21

**Formula Used:** LCM of Fractions = LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators (applied to simplified fractions)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/60a4d9941d944ee37bd4ba14741aa71996c9cab63ec977c4b749ca6ef2794366.png] 

⇒ First, **reduce** all fractions to their simplest forms:

⇒ Fraction 1 = 4/7

⇒ Fraction 2 = 8/14 = (8 ÷ 2) / (14 ÷ 2) = 4/7

⇒ Fraction 3 = 12/21 = (12 ÷ 3) / (21 ÷ 3) = 4/7

⇒ Now, find the **LCM** of (4/7, 4/7, 4/7):

⇒ LCM = LCM of (4, 4, 4) ÷ HCF of (7, 7, 7)

⇒ LCM = 4 ÷ 7 = 4/7

**∴ The correct answer is 4/7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM of Fractions Formula

LCM of fractions = LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators. Ensure fractions are in their simplest form first.

HCF of Fractions Formula

HCF of fractions = HCF of Numerators ÷ LCM of Denominators. This is the inverse of the LCM rule.

Simplification Rule

For any LCM or HCF calculation involving fractions, failing to simplify fractions to their **lowest terms** (co-prime numerators and denominators) can lead to incorrect results.

questions.question: The ratio of two numbers is 4 : 5 and their Least Common Multiple is 180. What is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Ratio** of numbers = 4 : 5

**LCM** of ratio parts 4 and 5 = 20 units

Given 20 units = 180 ⇒ 1 unit = 9

**Sum** of ratios = 4 + 5 = 9 units

Total **Sum** = 9 × 9 = 81

**∴ The correct answer is 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Ratio** of two numbers = 4 : 5

**LCM** of the numbers = 180

**Formula Used:**

If two numbers are in the ratio a : b, then the numbers are ax and bx (where x is the **HCF**).

**LCM** (ax, bx) = a × b × x (if a and b are **coprime**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/04c73bda670afc761ae031ab1f8202ecf3d877251fc95e12f4740a0feaf55ebe.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 4x and 5x.

⇒ **LCM** of 4x and 5x = 4 × 5 × x = 20x

⇒ According to the question, 20x = 180

⇒ x = 180 ÷ 20

⇒ x = 9 (This is the **HCF** of the numbers)

⇒ First number = 4 × 9 = 36

⇒ Second number = 5 × 9 = 45

⇒ **Sum** of the numbers = 36 + 45 = 81

**∴ The correct answer is 81.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between LCM and HCF

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**: A × B = HCF × LCM.

HCF of Ratios

If numbers are in the ratio a : b, then the **HCF** is the common multiplier x that converts the ratio into actual values ax and bx.

Coprime Numbers

Two numbers are **coprime** if their **HCF** is 1. If ratio parts are simplified (like 4 and 5), they are always coprime.

questions.question: If 30 percent of a number is 90, then what will be the 120 percent of that number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **ratio** of the percentages is 30% : 120% = 1 : 4.

Given that 1 part (representing **30%**) is equal to **90**.

To find 4 parts (representing **120%**), we calculate: 4 × 90 = 360.

**∴ The correct answer is 360.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 30% of a **number** is 90.

**Formula:** Value = (Total Number × Percentage) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2361d8e89e72533761f6dd09d3dd775b829cb5c3aa622d69694cbb4ba1a327fc.png] 

⇒ Let the **number** be x.

⇒ 30% × x = 90

⇒ (30 ÷ 100) × x = 90

⇒ x = (90 × 100) ÷ 30

⇒ x = 300

⇒ Now, find 120% of the **number** 300:

⇒ 120% of 300 = (120 ÷ 100) × 300

⇒ 1.2 × 300 = 360

**∴ The correct answer is 360.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method in Percentage

If p% of a number is 'a', then 1% is a ÷ p, and q% is (a ÷ p) × q.

Percentage to Decimal Conversion

To convert a percentage to a decimal, divide by 100 (e.g., 120% = 120 ÷ 100 = 1.2).

Percentage of a Number

The formula to find p% of x is (p ÷ 100) × x.

questions.question: What is the value of 40 percent of 80 percent of 5/8 of 4800?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Convert **percentages** into **fractions**: 40% = 2/5 and 80% = 4/5.

Required value = (2/5) × (4/5) × (5/8) × 4800

Simplify fractions first: (4/5) × (5/8) = 1/2. Then (2/5) × (1/2) = 1/5.

Final calculation: 1/5 × 4800 = 960.

**∴ The correct answer is 960.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Initial value** = 4800, **fractional part** = 5/8, **percentages** = 80% and 40%.

**Formula Used:** Final Value = P₁% × P₂% × Fraction × Total Value

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b068a70308173141d25448c86af037d85497eaf37e4fb4fc21da995df9c51136.png] 

⇒ **Step 1:** Calculate 5/8 of 4800

⇒ (5/8) × 4800 = 5 × 600 = 3000

⇒ **Step 2:** Calculate 80% of the result

⇒ 80% of 3000 = (80/100) × 3000 = 0.8 × 3000 = 2400

⇒ **Step 3:** Calculate 40% of the result

⇒ 40% of 2400 = (40/100) × 2400 = 0.4 × 2400 = 960

**∴ The correct answer is 960.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The 'Of' Operator

In mathematical expressions, **'of'** functions as a **multiplication** sign and should be prioritized according to **BODMAS/VBODMAS** rules.

Percentage to Fraction Chart

Memorizing common equivalents helps in quick calculations: 20% = 1/5, 40% = 2/5, 60% = 3/5, 80% = 4/5, and 12.5% = 1/8.

Commutative Property of Multiplication

The order of multiplication does not affect the result. Therefore, (40% of 80% of 5/8) is identical to (5/8 of 40% of 80%).

questions.question: 40 percent of the cost price of an article is equal to the 50 percent of its selling price. What is the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Cost Price (CP)** to **Selling Price (SP)** is the inverse of their percentage coefficients.

CP : SP = 50 : 40 = 5 : 4

Since CP (5) > SP (4), there is a **Loss** of 1 unit.

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 40% of CP = 50% of SP

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/816e741860a003fd494b502f7e2194acee84f7d69ab501bcb543d054267e6178.png] 

**Formula:** Loss % = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100

⇒ 40 ÷ 100 × CP = 50 ÷ 100 × SP

⇒ 4 × CP = 5 × SP

⇒ SP ÷ CP = 4 ÷ 5

⇒ Let CP = 5 and SP = 4

⇒ Loss = 5 − 4 = 1

⇒ Loss % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit occurs when **Selling Price (SP)** > **Cost Price (CP)**. Profit % = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Inverse Ratio Property

If x% of A = y% of B, then the ratio A : B = y : x. This is a common shortcut for comparison-based problems.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

questions.question: A person earns 30 percent profit on selling price. What will be his profit percentage on the cost price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Profit** is 30% on **Selling Price (SP)** ⇒ Profit : SP = 30 : 100 = 3 : 10

Since **Cost Price (CP)** = SP − Profit, then CP = 10 − 3 = 7 units

**Profit percentage** on CP = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

Profit % = (3 ÷ 7) × 100 = 42.857...% ≈ 42.86%

**∴ The correct answer is 42.86 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Profit on **Selling Price** = 30%

**Formula Used:** Profit % on **Cost Price** = [Profit ÷ (Selling Price − Profit)] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b0d8f73e6f057cd41378a733cd68a0787c804a60d6d9297c32dae36a9ef2ee6.png] 

⇒ Let the **Selling Price (SP)** = 100

⇒ **Profit** earned = 30% of 100 = 30

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** = SP − Profit = 100 − 30 = 70

⇒ **Profit Percentage** on Cost Price = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (30 ÷ 70) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 300 ÷ 7 = 42.857...

⇒ Profit % ≈ 42.86%

**∴ The correct answer is 42.86 percent.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage Comparison

Profit % on **Cost Price** is always numerically **higher** than Profit % on **Selling Price** because the denominator (CP) is smaller than SP.

Direct Conversion Rule

If profit on SP is x%, then Profit % on CP = [x ÷ (100 − x)] × 100.

Loss on Selling Price

If loss on SP is y%, then Loss % on CP = [y ÷ (100 + y)] × 100.

questions.question: R is 40 percent more efficient than S. S alone can finish a work in 35 days. In how many days will R alone finish the same work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Efficiency ratio** of R : S = 140 : 100 = 7 : 5.

**Time ratio** is inversely proportional ⇒ R : S = 5 : 7.

Given S takes 35 days (7 units = 35 days ⇒ 1 unit = 5 days).

Time for R alone = 5 units × 5 = 25 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **S** = 35 days.

**R** is 40% more efficient than **S**.

**Formula used:**

Total Work = **Efficiency** × **Time**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c23016d4885446c0e8b219673905286afff3340e4342e8554b954421db2dca8.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **Efficiency of S** be 1 unit/day.

⇒ **Total Work** = 1 × 35 = 35 units.

⇒ **Efficiency of R** = 1 + 40% of 1 = 1.4 units/day.

⇒ **Time taken by R** = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of R

⇒ Time for R = 35 ÷ 1.4

⇒ Time for R = 350 ÷ 14 = 25 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relation

Efficiency is **inversely proportional** to the time taken to complete a task. If efficiency ratio is a : b, then time ratio is b : a.

Work and Wages

In most competitive exams, **wages** are distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual, which depends on their efficiency and time spent.

Percentage Conversion

To increase a value by x%, multiply the base value by (100 + x) ÷ 100. Here, 40% more means a multiplier of **1.4**.

questions.question: R alone can do a work in 10 days working 3 hours a day. S alone can do the same work in 6 days working 5 hours a day. How many hours do they need to work together in a day to complete the same work in 4 days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total hours for **R** = 10 × 3 = 30 hr | Total hours for **S** = 6 × 5 = 30 hr.

questions.question: S travels with 40 percent of his usual speed and reaches his home 15 minutes late. What is the usual time (in minutes) taken by him to reach home?

**Speed ratio** (Usual : New) = 100% : 40% = 5 : 2.

Since distance is constant, **Time ratio** is the inverse of speed ratio = 2 : 5.

Difference in time parts = 5 − 2 = 3 units.

Given, 3 units = 15 min ⇒ 1 unit = 5 min.

**Usual time** = 2 units = 2 × 5 = 10 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Let **Usual speed** = S and **Usual time** = T.

⇒ New Speed = 40% of S = 0.4S.

⇒ New Time = T + 15 min.

⇒ Since **Distance** is same: S × T = 0.4S × (T + 15)

⇒ T = 0.4T + 6

⇒ T − 0.4T = 6

⇒ 0.6T = 6

⇒ T = 6 ÷ 0.6 = 10 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 10 min.**

Late and Early Concept

Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?
Will the necessary arrangements be made by the organisers before the festival starts?

options.text: Do the organisers make the necessary arrangements before the festival starts?
Will the organisers make the necessary arrangements before the festival starts?
Have the organisers made the necessary arrangements before the festival starts?
Did the organisers make the necessary arrangements before the festival starts?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Will the organisers make the necessary arrangements before the festival starts?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence is in the **Passive Voice** and follows the structure of an **Interrogative Sentence** in the **Future Indefinite Tense** (Simple Future).

• The passive construction for simple future interrogative is: **Will/Shall + Object + be + V3 (Past Participle) + by + Subject?**. Here, the object is **the necessary arrangements** and the subject (agent) is **the organisers**.

• To convert this into **Active Voice**, the structure must change to: **Will/Shall + Subject + V1 (Base Form) + Object?**.

• Applying this rule, the subject **the organisers** moves to the beginning after the auxiliary verb **Will**, and the main verb **made** reverts to its base form **make**.

• The phrase **before the festival starts** is a subordinate clause that remains unchanged during the voice transformation.

• Therefore, the active form is: **Will the organisers make the necessary arrangements before the festival starts?**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Active vs. Passive Voice Rules:**

• **Active Voice:** The subject performs the action (e.g., **The organisers will make...**).

• **Passive Voice:** The subject receives the action (e.g., **Arrangements will be made...**).

• In **Future Indefinite**, the auxiliary **will** is accompanied by **be** in the passive form, while the main verb always takes the **third form (V3)**.

• Options using **Do**, **Have**, or **Did** are incorrect because they change the **Tense** of the sentence to **Simple Present**, **Present Perfect**, and **Simple Past** respectively.

• The auxiliary verb **Will** is used for third-person plural subjects like **the organisers** in modern English standard usage.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**reaffirmed his commitment**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb **reaffirm** is defined as stating or asserting something strongly **once again**. The prefix **re-** in English grammar inherently denotes **repetition** or a return to a previous state.
 
• Using the word **again** in conjunction with **reaffirmed** creates a **pleonasm**, which is the use of more words than are necessary to convey a meaning. This is considered a **redundancy error** in formal writing.
 
• In the original sentence, the phrase **reaffirmed again** essentially translates to **affirmed again again**, which is grammatically incorrect. Removing the word **again** streamlines the sentence and adheres to the rules of **grammatical economy**.
 
• The structure **reaffirmed his commitment** is the most **precise** and **concise** choice, maintaining the **Subject-Verb-Object** flow while effectively conveying that the **chairman** is stating his dedication a second time.

• **Redundant Phrases in English:**
 
 
• **Option 1 (reaffirmed his commitment again):** Moving the word **again** to the end of the phrase does not eliminate the **semantic overlap**. It remains redundant because the **re-** prefix already carries the meaning of **again**.
 
• **Option 2 (reiterated once again):** The verb **reiterate** means to say something **repeatedly** for emphasis. Combining it with **once again** creates an even more wordy and **redundant** expression than the original sentence.
 
• Common examples of similar errors include **return back**, **revert back**, **recede back**, and **repeat again**. In all these cases, the adverb (back/again) should be omitted for **grammatical correctness**.
